# Get-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryRule

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the network discovery rules that scan IP ranges for hosts and services.

## SYNTAX

### All (Default)

```
Get-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryRule [-Limit <int>] [-SortField <string[]>] [-Id <ulong[]>] [-DiscoveredHost <ZabbixReference<ZabbixDiscoveredHost>[]>] [-DiscoveredService <ZabbixReference<ZabbixDiscoveredService>[]>] [-SelectDHosts] [-SelectNetworkDiscoveryChecks] [-Editable] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-SortOrder <ZabbixSortOrder[]>] [-Search <Hashtable>] [-SearchByAny] [-StartSearch] [-ExcludeSearch] [-SearchWildcardsEnabled] [-CountOutput] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-First <UInt64>] [-Skip <UInt64>] [-IncludeTotalCount] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A network discovery rule scans IP ranges on a schedule with its checks and reports the hosts and services it finds, for discovery actions to act on. The Get-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryRule cmdlet reads them with drule.get: all of them up to -Limit, by name with -Name (* and ? are wildcards), by id with -Id or from the pipeline, or with the whole drule.get selection in -Filter. -DiscoveredHost and -DiscoveredService narrow the result to the network discovery rules of the objects given, each a name, an id or a piped object. It writes ZabbixNetworkDiscoveryRule objects, with their related objects when a -Select switch asks for them, or, with -CountOutput, the number of matches; it needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Get a discovery rule by name

```powershell
Get-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryRule -Name 'Local network' | Select-Object NetworkDiscoveryRuleId, Name, IPRange, Delay, Status
```

-Name matches the rule's name exactly; the result is a ZabbixNetworkDiscoveryRule record.

### Example 2: Get a rule with its checks

```powershell
Get-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryRule -Name 'Local network' -SelectNetworkDiscoveryChecks |
    ForEach-Object Checks | Select-Object NetworkDiscoveryCheckId, Type, Key, Unique
```

-SelectNetworkDiscoveryChecks adds the rule's checks (dchecks) as Checks.

### Example 3: Find rules by part of their range

```powershell
Get-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryRule -Search @{ iprange = '192.0.2.' } | Where-Object Name -in 'Local network', 'Office printers' |
    Select-Object Name, IPRange
```

-Search matches substrings of wire fields (here iprange); several rules come back in one call.

### Example 4: List the devices a rule has discovered

```powershell
Get-ZbxNetworkDiscoveryRule -Name 'Local network' -SelectDHosts |
    Select-Object Name, @{ n = 'Discovered'; e = { @($_.DiscoveredHosts).Count } }
```

-SelectDHosts adds the discovered hosts (dhosts); a rule that has not run yet, as here, has none.
